meta.description: Human-reviewed contributor queue. The bot reads this file and nothing else. Every entry is reviewed in a normal pull request, which is the point: an agent that decides at runtime what to build will duplicate, hallucinate, and file issues nobody can action.
notes: status: backlog    -> eligible only when complete and not explicitly gated; ready items come first
status: ready      -> eligible; the bot may file it when the cap allows
status: filed      -> the bot created it; the marker lives in the issue body
status: shipped    -> the bot may comment + close its own issue, naming the release
Only ready/backlog entries with complete bodies and auto_file not false are ever filed.
latest_release   -> the tag the close comment cites; empty means the bot will not close anything it filed
auto_file: false -> explicit maintainer gate; never filed automatically even if body is complete.
Ready tasks are preferred; complete ungated backlog tasks replenish available slots. Historical markers prevent re-filing closed work.
Maintainer authorized up to 10 open contributor tasks total, not 10 new issues daily; roadmap and growth publishers share the ceiling.
Optional not_before uses a UTC date; depends_on IDs must have manifest status shipped before selection. Both gates fail closed.
Agentic roadmap kickoff is 2026-11-03 UTC; actual filing also depends on caps, existing queue priority, historical dedupe, shipped prerequisites, and PR merge.

items.title: docs: document the doctor and brain commands that already exist
items.body:
## Context

`package.json` already ships `doctor` (`node scripts/setup.js --check`) and `brain` (`node scripts/braincheck.js`), and the README mentions neither. A newcomer with a misconfigured model has no documented way to diagnose it.

## What to change

- `README.md`: after the install block, add `npm run doctor` and `npm run brain`, one line each on what they check.
- `docs/GUIDE.md`: add a "When something is wrong" subsection pointing at both.

Docs only; do not touch `src/` or `scripts/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run doctor` appears in `README.md` and `docs/GUIDE.md`
- [ ] Both are described from real output you ran yourself
- [ ] `node --test` still passes

## How to verify

```bash
node scripts/setup.js --check
node scripts/braincheck.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. The "Install it in two commands" block near the top of `README.md`.
2. The configuration section of `docs/GUIDE.md`.

## Time estimate

~1-2 hours.

items.title: test(security): prove resolveInWorkspace() refuses a symlink escape
items.body:
## Context

`src/tools.js:90` defines `resolveInWorkspace()`, and the README makes a security claim about it: files are confined to `QUASNOOZE_WORKSPACE` through `realpath()`, so a symlink cannot walk out. That claim has no targeted regression test.

Run the case by hand first. If the guard does **not** hold, stop and report it privately per `SECURITY.md` instead of opening a public PR.

## What to change

- `test/hardening.test.js`: add a test that creates a temp workspace, plants a symlink pointing outside it, and asserts `resolveInWorkspace()` refuses the path.
- Use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`. No new dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test fails if `realpath()` confinement is removed (check by patching temporarily, then revert)
- [ ] Temp directory cleaned up in a `finally` block
- [ ] Passes on Node 22, 24 and 26
- [ ] Test name states the guarantee, not the implementation

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/hardening.test.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. `src/tools.js:90` - `resolveInWorkspace()`, about 30 lines.
2. `test/hardening.test.js` - copy the setup/teardown pattern from the nearest case.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: test(cli): cover --version and an unknown verb in a smoke test
items.body:
## Context

`bin/pinch.js` is the entry point every user touches, and `scripts/growth.js` already carries a CLI-drift collector because promised verbs have drifted from implemented ones before. There is still no test that runs the CLI and asserts `--version` and an unknown verb behave sanely.

## What to change

- `test/cli.test.js` (new): via `node:child_process` `execFile` (argv array, never a shell string),
  1. `--version` exits 0 and prints the `package.json` version;
  2. an unknown verb exits non-zero or prints usage - assert whichever it does today and say which in the name;
  3. `help` prints a usage line containing a real verb.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No hard-coded version string; read it from `package.json`
- [ ] `execFile` with an argv array
- [ ] Passes on Node 22, 24, 26
- [ ] `node --test` still fully green

## How to verify

```bash
node bin/pinch.js --version
node bin/pinch.js help
node bin/pinch.js nope; echo "exit=$?"
node --test test/cli.test.js
```

## Where to start

1. `bin/pinch.js` - the verb `switch` and `usage()`.
2. `test/tools.test.js` - the existing spawn style.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: feat(memory): search local conversation history across sessions
items.body:
## Context

`docs/CAPABILITIES.json` marks `conversation-search` as `missing` (`src/store.js` lists and loads sessions by ID, never searches them). Because Quasnooze keeps every session on disk as plain atomic JSON under `data/sessions/`, searching past conversations requires zero external dependencies.

## What to change

- `src/store.js`: add `searchSessions(query, { limit = 10 } = {})` returning matching turns (`{ sessionId, role, snippet, ts }`) sorted newest-first, confined strictly inside `data/sessions/`.
- `src/tools.js`: expose a read-only `search_history` tool (`dangerous: false`) that delegates to `searchSessions` and registers matched sessions in `src/sources.js` so citations stay verifiable.
- `test/batch2.test.js`: cover multi-session substring/case-insensitive search, empty-query refusal, and snippet truncation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `searchSessions()` reads only inside `data/sessions/` and returns bounded snippets (`<= 240` chars)
- [ ] `search_history` is non-dangerous (read-only) and requires zero external packages
- [ ] Empty or whitespace-only queries return an empty array without scanning disk
- [ ] Unit tests pass on Node 22, 24, and 26, and `node scripts/audit.js` stays green

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/batch2.test.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. `src/store.js` — inspect how sessions are listed and cached.
2. `src/tools.js` — follow the `recall` tool shape.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: feat(telegram): preserve reply_to_message context in multi-turn chats
items.body:
## Context

`src/channels/telegram.js` polls `getUpdates` and routes `msg.text` directly to `routeMessage()`. When a user swipe-replies to an older Telegram message (`msg.reply_to_message`), that quoted text is dropped, so the assistant loses which message "do that again" or "summarize this" refers to.

## What to change

- `src/channels/telegram.js`: extract a pure helper `formatIncomingTelegramText(msg)` that prepends a bounded `[Replying to: "..."]\n` header (capped at 400 chars) when `msg.reply_to_message?.text` or `caption` is present, while leaving approval words (`yes`/`no`) untouched when replying to an approval prompt.
- `test/runtime.test.js`: add unit tests covering plain messages, quoted replies, oversized quoted text truncation, and approval replies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Quoted Telegram replies include a bounded `[Replying to: ...]` prefix (`<= 400` chars)
- [ ] Replying `yes` or `no` to an approval prompt still resolves the pending approval cleanly
- [ ] Pure helper exported and tested without network calls
- [ ] `node --test` and `node scripts/audit.js` pass

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/runtime.test.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. `src/channels/telegram.js` — update loop around `routeMessage({ channel: "telegram", ... })`.
2. `src/channels/router.js` — check how `YES` / `NO` approval replies are matched.

## Time estimate

~2 hours.

items.title: feat(voice): validate audio uploads, enforce Whisper timeout, and report voice status in doctor
items.body:
## Context

## What to change

- `src/server.js`: enforce a bounded timeout and supported audio MIME/size check on voice transcription requests, returning actionable JSON errors (`413` / `415` / `502` with clear message) when `WHISPER_URL` times out or is unset.
- `scripts/setup.js`: in `--check` (`npm run doctor`), report whether `WHISPER_URL` is configured and reachable (failing soft when unset, warning clearly when unreachable).
- `test/http-surface.test.js`: test unset `WHISPER_URL`, unsupported MIME, and upstream timeout handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Oversized or non-audio payloads are rejected with `413` / `415` before contacting `WHISPER_URL`
- [ ] Upstream Whisper hang aborts cleanly within a bounded deadline without crashing the server
- [ ] `node scripts/setup.js --check` reports voice configuration state accurately
- [ ] `node --test` and `node scripts/audit.js` pass

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/http-surface.test.js
node scripts/setup.js --check
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. `src/server.js` — search for `WHISPER_URL`.
2. `scripts/setup.js` — inspect the `--check` diagnostic output.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: fix(growth): normalize GitHub OPEN/CLOSED issue states before planning
items.body:
## Context

**Confirmed deterministic planner bug**, not a feature proposal. At baseline 7337971, plan() filters existing issues using state === "open". gh issue list --json uses uppercase OPEN/CLOSED, while REST uses lowercase. A synthetic call with one OPEN growth issue, maxOpen:1 and a qualifying candidate returns decision:file and "0 already open". No GitHub write is needed to reproduce. collectDemand(), decide() and historyFor() also compare raw state; audit them without changing demand/dedupe semantics. The shared board guard is separate: this task repairs the growth-specific cap and demand/history semantics.

Code inspected at commit `7337971114713b07dceae4ebfe399c6bec7c8bf4`:

items.body:
## Context

Existing path confinement and confirmation gates are not branch-level isolation; direct edits can affect the user’s working checkout.

## Upgraded design specification

Only in explicitly enabled coding mode, discover a Git root under an allowed workspace, inspect dirty/untracked files and existing worktrees, then offer a new generated branch and ignored, workspace-confined worktree using execFile argv (never shell interpolation). Bind file tools to that root, keep existing checks, pin base SHA, and ask separately before creation, merge, deletion or other dangerous operation. Refuse ambiguous, symlinked or outside-root locations, hooks/config surprises and unsupported submodules; surface manual recovery. A linked worktree is NOT an OS sandbox: shell, hooks, network, shared Git metadata and test scripts may access the host. Do not advertise containment or run untrusted repo code automatically.

- `src/agent/worktree.js (new)`

- [ ] Traversal, symlink escape, branch-name injection and missing Git fail closed; existing approval rules still apply.
- [ ] No command, hook, install or test runs without its existing explicit approval; unattended mode refuses dangerous actions.

items.title: feat(eval): offline workflow metrics and capability inventory checks
items.body:
## Context

Growth already measures repository signals, but coding workflow adoption, failure modes and evidence-backed capability changes have no focused offline inventory.

## Upgraded design specification

Aggregate only opted-in local counters (started, completed, blocked, verification status, approval denial and duration buckets) from redacted receipts with retention/deletion controls. Keep metrics local, off by default, and never send task content, paths, prompts or identifiers. Update capability inventory only as features actually ship; extend existing deterministic collectors with fixture-based checks for stale or missing evidence without model-generated issue churn.

## Affected files / modules

- `src/eval/workflow-metrics.js (new)`
- `scripts/growth.js`
- `docs/CAPABILITIES.json`
- `test/workflow-metrics.test.js (new)`
- `test/growth.test.js`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disabled metrics write nothing; enabled counters contain no prompts, paths, credentials, tool output or unique user identifiers.
- [ ] Fixture with missing evidence yields one deterministic report candidate and no direct GitHub write.
- [ ] Inventory claims link to existing files/tests; growth caps, fingerprints and maintainer review remain intact.

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/workflow-metrics.test.js test/growth.test.js test/market.test.js
```

Use `node:test` with temporary directories and deterministic fakes; no real secrets, external service or model required. Implement tests first and demonstrate the expected failure before the fix.

## Time estimate

2–3 engineer-days.

## Dependencies and release window

Week 4; not before 2026-11-24 UTC. Prerequisites: `agentic-02-evidence-ledger` (shipped).

items.title: feat(agent): safe resume after context trimming and process restart
items.body:
## Context

Budget fitting can discard conversation history and a restart loses the live state needed to safely continue a multi-step workflow.

## Upgraded design specification

Reconstruct a small data-only checkpoint from the local ledger: approved plan revision, current phase, active skill IDs, bounded recent evidence and constraints. Reapply authoritative system policy first; treat checkpoint and repository content as untrusted data. After restart require explicit resume and reapproval of pending side effects, revalidate worktree/revision and never replay a pending tool call.

## Affected files / modules

- `src/agent/resume.js (new)`
- `src/agent/ledger.js (new)`
- `src/budget.js`
- `src/agent.js`
- `test/agent-resume.test.js (new)`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After simulated trimming the system policy and active approved constraints remain within the context budget.
- [ ] Restart during a pending dangerous operation produces paused state and zero tool executions until new approval.
- [ ] Stale or corrupted checkpoints, changed base and session mismatch fail closed without cross-session disclosure.

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/agent-resume.test.js test/agent.test.js
```

Use `node:test` with temporary directories and deterministic fakes; no real secrets, external service or model required. Implement tests first and demonstrate the expected failure before the fix.

## Time estimate

2–3 engineer-days.

## Dependencies and release window

Week 4; not before 2026-11-24 UTC. Prerequisites: `agentic-02-evidence-ledger` (shipped), `agentic-05-skills` (shipped), `agentic-07-review` (shipped).

items.title: test(agent): offline end-to-end safety and rollout gate
items.body:
## Context

The proposed modules need an integrated offline regression and a product-safe rollout before their behavior can be claimed as shipped.

## Upgraded design specification

Keep the workflow behind an explicit default-off setting. Build a mock-brain, temporary Git repository end-to-end test spanning consent, plan, test failure/pass, review, handoff and cleanup refusal. Exercise session-bound approvals, no cloud fallback, no unauthorized side effects, cancellation and restart; document exact limitations and update inventory only for implemented behaviors. On Node 22, 24 and 26 run full test suite and audit.

## Affected files / modules

- `test/agent-workflow-e2e.test.js (new)`
- `docs/CAPABILITIES.json`
- `docs/GUIDE.md`
- `src/config.js`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With feature disabled existing conversation, tools, approvals and scheduler behaviors are unchanged.
- [ ] With feature enabled fake model and local Git complete the happy path without internet or an Ollama server; denial, malicious skill, stale evidence and crash paths stay blocked.
- [ ] CI runs node --test and node scripts/audit.js on supported Node versions; docs explicitly state worktrees are not a security sandbox.

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/agent-workflow-e2e.test.js && node --test && node scripts/audit.js
```

Use `node:test` with temporary directories and deterministic fakes; no real secrets, external service or model required. Implement tests first and demonstrate the expected failure before the fix.

## Time estimate

3–4 engineer-days.

## Dependencies and release window

Week 4; not before 2026-11-24 UTC. Prerequisites: `agentic-04-tdd` (shipped), `agentic-07-review` (shipped), `agentic-08-finish` (shipped), `agentic-09-debug` (shipped), `agentic-10-metrics` (shipped), `agentic-11-resume` (shipped).
